name: Customer accounts, their users and the representatives who impersonate them

mcpOnly.reason: No MCP tool documented in this repo sets a user-and-group type, a password or an impersonation grant, and the create_users, save_user_groups and assign_users_to_group argument shapes are not documented here; those bindings are planned.

hosted.reason: The group type and the impersonation grant are read back only through local SQL in this repo; a hosted install verifies users and passwords but those steps stay BLOCKED until an MCP or Management API read of them is documented.

steps.title: Ensure each user group by name, with its customer number

bindings.reason: save_user_groups members id, name, parentGroupId and customerNumber are documented (user-group-operations.md 17b) but the request member that carries the groups is not; read it from the tool's tools/list input schema, record it in that reference, then promote.
GroupSave is a whole-entity save whose full model is assembled from get_user_groups and the stored row; no create model is documented, and a fragment blanks what it omits.

steps.trap: save_user_groups is a whole-entity save against the cache: a column outside its model is written back as the model default (it blanked AccessUserRedirectOnLogin).

steps.title: Make each account group a root group of type SystemAccount

bindings.query: SELECT AccessUserId AS id, AccessUserParentId AS parentId, AccessUserUserAndGroupType AS groupType FROM AccessUser WHERE AccessUserId = @groupId

bindings.reason: The type is written only by a GroupSave full-model round trip (no MCP tool has a type member); the full model shape is not documented in this repo.

steps.trap: A B2B account group lists on the storefront CSR Accounts page only at root with the type SystemAccount; save_user_groups leaves the type NULL, which is right for a DC scoping group and wrong for an account.

steps.title: Ensure each user by user name, carrying the account's customer number

bindings.reason: create_users is named for creating logins with a customerNumber (dc-scoping.md) but its argument shape is not documented in this repo; read it from tools/list, record it, then promote.
UserSave is documented only as a UserById round trip; no create model is documented.

steps.trap: update_users is a whole-entity save from the cache: it writes back every modelled column from the cached value, so it reverts a SQL write made on the same row.

steps.title: Set the password of each login this run created
steps.trap: create_users and UserSave set no password (UserSave accepts one and drops it); the key member of UserSetPassword is userId, not id. The password is set only when the login is created: no read returns it, so a re-run never rotates an existing persona's password.

steps.title: Make each user a direct member of its group

bindings.reason: get_users_by_group_id is named for listing an account's contacts but its argument name is not documented in this repo.

bindings.query: SELECT AccessUserGroupRelationUserId AS userId, AccessUserGroupRelationGroupId AS groupId FROM AccessUserGroupRelation WHERE AccessUserGroupRelationUserId = @userId AND AccessUserGroupRelationGroupId = @groupId

readBack.query: SELECT AccessUserGroupRelationUserId AS userId, AccessUserGroupRelationGroupId AS groupId FROM AccessUserGroupRelation WHERE AccessUserGroupRelationUserId = @userId AND AccessUserGroupRelationGroupId = @groupId

bindings.reason: assign_users_to_group takes the pair directly, but its member names are not documented in this repo.

steps.trap: UserGroupRelationSave is a list command: the single {GroupId, UserId} shape answers HTTP 200 'No items selected' and writes nothing.

steps.title: Grant each representative impersonation of each customer, in that direction

bindings.reason: get_impersonatable_users needs an impersonator id input whose argument name is not documented in this repo.

bindings.query: SELECT AccessUserSecondaryRelationUserId AS impersonatorId, AccessUserSecondaryRelationSecondaryUserId AS customerId FROM AccessUserSecondaryRelation WHERE AccessUserSecondaryRelationUserId = @impersonatorId AND AccessUserSecondaryRelationSecondaryUserId = @customerId

readBack.query: SELECT AccessUserSecondaryRelationUserId AS impersonatorId, AccessUserSecondaryRelationSecondaryUserId AS customerId FROM AccessUserSecondaryRelation WHERE AccessUserSecondaryRelationUserId = @impersonatorId AND AccessUserSecondaryRelationSecondaryUserId = @customerId

bindings.reason: add_impersonatable_users is named as the in-product grant (order-lifecycle.md) but its argument shape is not documented in this repo.

steps.trap: One grant is one AccessUserSecondaryRelation row: UserId is the impersonator, SecondaryUserId the customer. The wrong direction is quiet: an empty impersonation bar, and the representative listed under 'Users that can impersonate this user' on the customer.

probes.title: Every user of an account carries the account's customer number
Every user is a direct member of its group

bindings.reason: get_users_by_group_id argument name is not documented in this repo.

bindings.query: SELECT AccessUserGroupRelationUserId AS userId, AccessUserGroupRelationGroupId AS groupId FROM AccessUserGroupRelation WHERE AccessUserGroupRelationUserId = @userId AND AccessUserGroupRelationGroupId = @groupId

probes.title: Each grant reads impersonator to customer

bindings.query: SELECT AccessUserSecondaryRelationUserId AS impersonatorId FROM AccessUserSecondaryRelation WHERE AccessUserSecondaryRelationUserId = @impersonatorId AND AccessUserSecondaryRelationSecondaryUserId = @customerId

probes.title: No grant reads customer to impersonator

bindings.query: SELECT AccessUserSecondaryRelationUserId AS impersonatorId FROM AccessUserSecondaryRelation WHERE AccessUserSecondaryRelationUserId = @customerId AND AccessUserSecondaryRelationSecondaryUserId = @impersonatorId

probes.title: Each persona in DW_PERSONA_CREDENTIALS signs in and is served as itself

traps: No surface sets a password on create: create_users has no password member and UserSave drops one; UserSetPassword (key userId) sets it, and only a sign-in proves it.

An impersonation grant is not observable until the Users index is rebuilt: the user-index extender copies the relation onto the user documents, and nothing marks them dirty. Flush UserService and run a Full build of Users.index under both Users and Secondary users.
The CSR Accounts list shows an account group only at root with the user-and-group type SystemAccount; a DC scoping group wants the type left NULL.
A refusal on these surfaces arrives as HTTP 200 (status invalid, No items selected): assert the relation or the row, never the status.
UserDelete on a group id answers ok and deletes nothing; GroupDelete deletes groups.
